assumptions_or_open_questions: Option A (DIC + alkalinity as state, derive CO2/HCO3/CO3/pH each tick) is the recommended approach since both DIC and alkalinity are already canonical state variables. Confirm this before proceeding.

The analytical closed-form solver is sufficient for the freshwater aquarium pH range (5.5-8.5) with CO2-only weak-acid system. No Newton-Raphson iteration is needed unless other weak acids (humic, phosphoric) are added later.
pKa1 temperature correction (pKa1(T) ≈ 6.352 - 0.0238 × (T-25)) is adequate for 15-35°C. pKa2 correction may be deferred since CO3-- is negligible below pH ~8 in aquarium conditions.

The existing bicarbonate_mg_total field in WaterState is currently stored but not solved from equilibrium — the design note must clarify whether this field becomes a derived value overwritten each tick or is deprecated in favor of a speciation struct.

CO2 gas exchange (Henry's law, surface aeration) is explicitly out of scope for this first-pass design note but the contract should not preclude it. The design should note where gas exchange would plug in.

The design note should specify precision expectations: e.g., pH accuracy within ±0.05 of a reference implementation across the 5.5-8.5 range, and whether the solver output should be validated against published carbonate tables.

Source-water presets will need updated DIC/alkalinity values or a note explaining that the current values should produce differentiated pH once the real solver replaces the shortcut. This is a downstream consequence, not part of the design note itself.
data.problem_framing: The simulator needs a design note that defines the carbonate-state contract before implementation can proceed. Currently, pH is computed via an empirical shortcut (chemistry.rs:18: `6.3 + log10(alk) - log10(DIC)`) that does not use equilibrium constants, ignores temperature dependence, and collapses four shipped source-water presets to nearly identical pH (6.30-6.33). The project already tracks DIC (mg C total) and alkalinity (meq total) as explicit state in WaterState, and temperature_c is available. The design note must specify: (1) which variables are explicit state vs derived from equilibrium, (2) the solver approach and its numerical properties, (3) temperature dependence of pKa values, (4) update order within the hourly chemistry step, (5) what is intentionally excluded in the first pass. Three existing docs need updates: scientific_inventory.md (pool catalog entries for DIC, alkalinity, bicarbonate, pH), UNITS.md (naming policy for any new derived quantities like CO2_aq or speciated carbonate), and scientific_specs.md (the v0.3 roadmap section now becomes concrete). The design note itself is the primary deliverable and will live as a new file in docs/.

proposed_work.details: Create a new design document covering: (1) State contract — DIC (mg C total) and alkalinity (meq total) remain explicit state; CO2(aq), HCO3-, CO3--, and pH are derived each tick via equilibrium. Temperature is read from WaterState. (2) Equilibrium equations — the two dissociation reactions with pKa1 ≈ 6.35 and pKa2 ≈ 10.33 at 25°C, the alkalinity definition (Alk = [HCO3-] + 2[CO3--] + [OH-] - [H+]), and the DIC conservation equation (DIC = [CO2(aq)] + [HCO3-] + [CO3--]). (3) Solver strategy — analytical closed-form: given DIC_mmol_L, Alk_meq_L, and temperature-adjusted Ka1/Ka2, solve the charge-balance polynomial for [H+]. For the pH 5.5-8.5 range with CO2-only system, this reduces to a quadratic or cubic that can be solved directly. Document the specific algebraic derivation. (4) Temperature dependence — pKa1(T) ≈ 6.352 - 0.0238 × (T-25), pKa2(T) ≈ 10.329 - 0.0188 × (T-25). Note that pKa2 correction is included for completeness but CO3-- contribution is small in the target range. (5) Update order — compute_carbonate_equilibrium(dic_total, alk_total, temp_c, volume_l) returns a CarbonateEquilibrium struct containing co2_aq_mmol_l, hco3_mmol_l, co3_mmol_l, ph, and optionally updates the stored bicarbonate_mg_total field. Called once per hourly chemistry step, after DIC/alkalinity modifications from respiration/photosynthesis/nitrification. (6) Stability expectations — no iteration, O(1) per call, deterministic. pH output clamped to 4.0-10.0 as a safety net. (7) Explicit exclusions — no CO2 gas exchange, no CO2 injection hardware, no other weak acids (humic, phosphoric), no mineral precipitation/dissolution, no ionic-strength corrections. Note where each would plug in.

risks: The analytical closed-form solver assumes a CO2-only weak-acid system. If the simulator later adds humic acids, phosphoric acid buffering, or other weak acids, the solver will need to be upgraded to iterative (Newton-Raphson). The design note should document this boundary explicitly so the upgrade path is clear.

The existing bicarbonate_mg_total field is currently an independent state variable set from source-water profiles. Making it solver-derived changes its semantics: water changes that bring in bicarbonate_mg_per_l will need to update DIC and alkalinity instead, or the materialization path needs adjustment. This is an implementation concern for tanksim-6e5.4.2 but the design note must call it out.

The linear pKa temperature approximations (pKa1(T) ≈ 6.352 - 0.0238 × (T-25)) are adequate for 15-35°C but diverge outside that range. If the simulator supports extreme temperatures (e.g., cold-water tanks below 10°C), a more accurate empirical formula (Harned & Davis, Plummer & Busenberg) would be needed.

Source-water preset DIC/alkalinity ratios may need recalibration after the solver replaces the shortcut, since the shortcut's empirical 6.3 offset masked the true equilibrium pH. The current presets may produce unexpected pH values with the real solver. This is downstream of the design note but should be flagged.
